[1] (atlas-sync-manual.pdf, page 1)
Atlas Sync Manual - Overview and Installation Atlas Sync is a command-line tool that copies files between a laptop and a storage bucket. This manual describes a fictional product used to test the knowledge assistant. Atlas Sync requires Python 3.10 or newer. Install it with pip install atlas-sync. The installer creates a configuration folder at ~/.atlas. Run atlas init to create a default configuration file named atlas.toml. System requirements: at least 512 MB of free memory and 2 GB of free disk space for the local cache.

[2] (atlas-sync-manual.pdf, page 2)
Configuration The configuration file atlas.toml contains the following keys. sync_interval sets how often Atlas checks for changes, in seconds. The default is 300 seconds. max_upload_mb limits the size of a single file upload. The default is 250 MB; larger files are skipped with a warning. retry_limit controls how many times a failed transfer is retried. The default is 5 attempts with exponential backoff. cache_dir sets the folder used for the local cache. The default is ~/.atlas/cache. encryption can be set to aes256 or none. When it is set to aes256, files are encrypted on the laptop before upload. bandwidth_limit caps the upload speed in kilobytes per second; 0 means unlimited.

[3] (atlas-sync-manual.pdf, page 4)
Error Codes E1001: the configuration file atlas.toml could not be found. Run atlas init. E1007: the access token has expired. Run atlas login again. E1042: the local cache is full. Run atlas prune or increase the space available to cache_dir. E1043: a file exceeded max_upload_mb and was skipped. E1050: the network connection was lost during a transfer. Atlas retries up to retry_limit times. E2001: atlas verify found a checksum mismatch. The remote copy is uploaded again on the next push. E3000: the bucket does not exist or the account has no permission to write to it.

# Embeddings and Vector Search ## What an embedding is An embedding model maps a piece of text to a fixed-length list of numbers called a vector. The model all-MiniLM-L6-v2 produces vectors with 384 dimensions and was trained on over one billion sentence pairs. Texts with similar meaning are mapped to vectors that point in similar directions. ## Normalisation Vectors are usually normalised to length one. For normalised vectors, cosine similarity and dot product give the same ranking, and squared Euclidean distance equals two minus two times the cosine similarity. ## Approximate nearest neighbour search Comparing a question with every stored vector is called brute-force or exact search, and it becomes slow for millions of vectors. # Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) Basics Retrieval-augmented generation is a way to make a language model answer questions about documents it was never trained on. Instead of relying on what the model memorised, the system first retrieves relevant passages and then asks the model to answer using only those passages. ## The pipeline A RAG system has two phases. In the indexing phase, documents are split into chunks, each chunk is converted into an embedding vector, and the vectors are stored in a vector database. In the query phase, the user's question is embedded with the same model, the closest chunks are retrieved, and the language model writes an answer from them. ## Chunking Chunk size controls how much text goes into each piece. # Deploying and Operating an AI Service ## Containers Docker packages an application with its dependencies into an image, so it runs the same way on a laptop and on a server. A Dockerfile lists the steps to build the image, and docker compose starts several containers together, such as an API and a model server. ## Continuous integration A CI pipeline such as GitHub Actions runs linting and tests on every push. A quality gate is a CI step that fails the build when a metric drops below a threshold, for example when Recall@5 falls under 0.8. ## Latency percentiles p50 is the median latency: half of all requests are faster. p95 is the latency that 95 percent of requests are faster than, and it reveals slow outliers that an average hides. ## Caching Caching the embeddings of repeated

that 95 percent of requests are faster than, and it reveals slow outliers that an average hides. ## Caching Caching the embeddings of repeated questions avoids recomputing them. Caching full answers is riskier, because answers must change when documents change. ## Authentication JSON Web Tokens (JWT) are signed tokens that prove who a user is. The server signs each token with a secret key, and the token includes an expiry time, after which the user must log in again. Passwords must be stored as slow salted hashes such as Argon2, never as plain text. ## Observability Logging each request's question, retrieved chunk IDs, latency and token counts makes it possible to debug wrong answers and to spot regressions.

# Large Language Model Basics ## Tokens Language models read and write text as tokens, which are pieces of words. In English, one token is roughly four characters, or about three quarters of a word. ## Context window The context window is the maximum number of tokens the model can read in one request, including the prompt, the retrieved passages and the answer. Passages that do not fit must be dropped, which is why retrieving the right passages matters more than retrieving many of them. ## Temperature Temperature controls randomness. A temperature of 0 makes the model pick the most likely token each time, giving repeatable answers, which is useful for evaluation. Higher temperatures produce more varied text. ## Hallucination A hallucination is a fluent statement that is not supported by

[2] (rag-basics.md, page 1)
model writes an answer from them. ## Chunking Chunk size controls how much text goes into each piece. Small chunks are precise but can lose context; large chunks keep context but dilute relevance. Chunk overlap repeats a few hundred characters between neighbouring chunks so that a sentence cut at a boundary still appears complete in at least one chunk. ## Citations and refusals A grounded answer cites the passages it used, so a reader can check every claim. When no retrieved passage contains the answer, a well-behaved RAG system says "I don't know" instead of guessing. Answers that state facts not found in the sources are called hallucinations.

Commands atlas push uploads changed local files to the bucket. atlas pull downloads files that changed in the bucket since the last sync. atlas status shows pending changes and the time of the last successful sync. atlas verify compares checksums of local and remote files and reports mismatches. atlas prune --older-than 30d deletes cached copies older than 30 days. atlas login opens a browser window to sign in. The access token is stored in the system keychain and expires after 12 hours.

Atlas Sync Manual - Overview and Installation Atlas Sync is a command-line tool that copies files between a laptop and a storage bucket. This manual describes a fictional product used to test the knowledge assistant. Atlas Sync requires Python 3.10 or newer. Install it with pip install atlas-sync. The installer creates a configuration folder at ~/.atlas. Run atlas init to create a default configuration file named atlas.toml. System requirements: at least 512 MB of free memory and 2 GB of free disk space for the local cache.

[2] (atlas-sync-manual.pdf, page 4)
Error Codes E1001: the configuration file atlas.toml could not be found. Run atlas init. E1007: the access token has expired. Run atlas login again. E1042: the local cache is full. Run atlas prune or increase the space available to cache_dir. E1043: a file exceeded max_upload_mb and was skipped. E1050: the network connection was lost during a transfer. Atlas retries up to retry_limit times. E2001: atlas verify found a checksum mismatch. The remote copy is uploaded again on the next push. E3000: the bucket does not exist or the account has no permission to write to it.

[3] (atlas-sync-manual.pdf, page 2)
Configuration The configuration file atlas.toml contains the following keys. sync_interval sets how often Atlas checks for changes, in seconds. The default is 300 seconds. max_upload_mb limits the size of a single file upload. The default is 250 MB; larger files are skipped with a warning. retry_limit controls how many times a failed transfer is retried. The default is 5 attempts with exponential backoff. cache_dir sets the folder used for the local cache. The default is ~/.atlas/cache. encryption can be set to aes256 or none. When it is set to aes256, files are encrypted on the laptop before upload. bandwidth_limit caps the upload speed in kilobytes per second; 0 means unlimited.
